title: fix(app-shell): show a position's label in a permission set's Assigned users (objectui#13477)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D2bmCsjnmZkrozUjaCZ8Xgr)_

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer)

Fixes #13477

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changed

`AssignedUsersSection` (a permission set's Assigned users list) drew each "via position" chip from the holder's `sys_user_position.position`, the position's machine name, through `c.viaPosition(v.position)`. The same `load` already lists the registry's position definitions through `ensureType('position')` to find the positions that distribute the set, and that list carries each definition's `label` as `/meta/position` serves it in the caller's language (objectstack#25701).

- A module-private `positionLabels(positions)` reads `name` to `label` from that one list (a blank or non-string label is skipped).
- Each position entry of a row's `via` now carries `label` beside `position`.
- The chip text is `c.viaPosition(label ?? name)`, and the chip's `title` is the machine name whenever the text is not the name, the same rule `CitedItemChip` in `AccessExplainPanel` applies. With no label the chip reads by its name and has no `title`, as before.
- No new read: the label comes from the list the section already fetched.
- `.changeset/13477-assigned-users-position-label.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell` patch.

Files: `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AssignedUsersSection.tsx`, its existing test `AssignedUsersSection.test.tsx` (the fixture's `contributor` definition has the label `Contributor`, so the chip assertion now reads `via position Contributor`), the new pin `AssignedUsersSection.positionLabel-13477.test.tsx`, and the changeset.

## Tests

The new pin mounts the real `AssignedUsersSection` inside the real `MetadataProvider`, over a real `ObjectStackAdapter` whose `fetch` is the only stub, so the label reaches the chip through the store's own `GET /api/v1/meta/position`:

- `shows the label from /meta/position, with the machine name on title`: chip `via position Sales Manager`, `title="sales_manager"`, and no `via position sales_manager`.
- `a definition with no label reads by its name, with no title`: chip `via position field_rep` with no `title`, beside the labelled one.

Readings, taken locally on the branch head:

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AssignedUsersSection`: Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 29 passed (29).
- Nearby: the same plus `PositionHoldersSection` and `AccessExplainPanel` prefixes: Test Files 14 passed (14), Tests 84 passed (84).
- Reverse check (fix committed, then only `AssignedUsersSection.tsx` put back to the base commit): both new tests and the updated chip assertion in `AssignedUsersSection.test.tsx` fail (3 failed, 11 passed across the two files); with the fix restored they pass.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the three touched source/test files: 0 errors, 15 warnings. Each warning is a rule on a line this branch did not write (`no-explicit-any`, `react-hooks/refs`, `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, and `only-export-components` on the existing `positionsDistributing` export). The new helper stays unexported so it adds none.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: pass, 1 changeset declared for the 1 released package.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations.

## Acceptance notes

The sweep looked for any other site that draws a raw position or permission-set machine name from a payload other than the `/meta/position` or `/meta/permission` list. The brief allowed a fix in the same diff only where the fix is the same one-line label lookup from a list that component already loads. None of the sites below qualified, so this diff touches none of them.

Already labelled, nothing to do:

- `PositionHoldersSection` (a position's holders) lists people only. It draws no position or permission-set name.
- Approver `type: 'position'` (the `decision_output_defs` entry in `apps/console/src/services/approvalsApi.ts`): the decide dialog's picker is built by `registryOptions` in `decisionOutputParams.ts` from `ensureType('position')`, using `label` and falling back to the name. Approver display goes through `useApproverDirectory`, whose registry leg labels `position:` references from the same store read.
- `AccessExplainPanel` Principal card and "Contributed by" chips already label through `CitedItemChip`.

Raw names that remain, each needing more than a one-line lookup (none of these components loads the list):

- Sharing-rule `sharedWith`: the catalog's "Shared with" list column (the `render` on the `sharedWith` column in `anchors.ts`) and the summary row in `SharingRuleCloneDialog` both print `TYPE: VALUE`, e.g. `position: sales_manager`. Neither loads `/meta/position`, and the recipient type itself is a raw token.
- `PositionGrantCells` (the position list's "Permission sets" column) draws `_grantedPermissionSets[].name` from the list's served `listInclude` column. The component loads no `/meta/permission` list.
- `PositionPreview` lists the draft definition's `permissionSets` as code-formatted machine names. It loads no permission list.
- Suggested bindings (`SuggestedBindingsPanel`, its Studio copy in `StudioDesignSurface`, and `MarketplacePackagePage` toasts) interpolate the suggestion payload's `permission_set_name` into their sentences. None of them loads `/meta/permission`.

Locale of the metadata store's reads: `MetadataProvider.ensureType` reads through `adapter.getClient().meta.getItems(type)`. The console's adapter is built in `AdapterProvider` with `createAuthenticatedFetch()`, which sets `Accept-Language` from `document.documentElement.lang` on every API call that does not already carry one. `ConnectedShellInner` keys `MetadataProvider` on the UI language (`key={language}`) and clears the adapter cache on a switch, so `/meta/position` and `/meta/permission` are read again in the new language. Nothing on this branch re-checks that wiring; it was read from the source and the new pin does not assert the header.
